newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 21.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Inflation is estimated to fall to 6.3 percent in March, sources at the national economy ministry say, down from 6.6 percent the previous month and boosting the market's confidence in the governmen's economic policies.

--Yesterday's inner cabinet meeting examined wage increases for public organisations and bodies (DEKO) and the government's announcement that they not exceed 7.0 percent. A committee is expected to be set up to monitor increases.
--Changes to tax offices and services will be instituted in June and will be based on performances of each office in reaching projected targets.
--The Capital Market Commission continues to impose fines on those involved in last year's Delta scandal: yesterday fines totalling 450 million drachmas were imposed on a number of brokers.

--A breach betweeen the state and the Olympic Metro consortium building the Athens Metro system after the meeting yesterday with Environment, Town Planning and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis. The consortium is demanding another 82 billion drachmas.
--Forex loans will carry a further 1.0 percent charge on their interest rates, in an effort to crub increasing demand for forex loans causing excessive fluidity.
--The state can expect revenues in the order of 18-20 billion drachmas from the taxation of foreign exchange deposits, finance ministry sources say.
--The Athens bourse yesterday approved the listing of Sfakianakis AEBE on the bourse's main market and an increase in share capital by public subscription.

--The Metro project will be reduced by some 1,900 metres following Laliotis's announcement that the state would not enter satisfy non-contractural demands by the consortium. He warned that the state's patience with these demands was running out.
--European Commission President Jacques Santer will attend the Northern Greek Federation of Industries general assembly on May 9 in the northern port city.

--Greece's economic diplomacy in the Balkans is believed to be a building block for political stability in the region and consolidate a leading position for Greece. Prime Minister Costas Simitis's visit to Romania today is a precursor to these efforts.
--The development ministry is not prioritising a withdrawal of licences or imposition of other restrictions on insurance firms at this time.
